title: The Sustained Breach · The Eye and the Altar
dek: Strangers meet under an immense watching eye. A meteor strike destabilizes the breach, and the survivors find an altar and map that turn their escape into evidence of a planned opening.

facts.Recorded dates: Source posts · 17 July 2026 · in-world date unresolved
facts.Outcome: Immediate enemies fall; separate tears provide exits. An altar, map and notes establish deliberate preparation for this breach. The eye’s identity and complete ritual purpose remain unknown.

body:
A breach visible from an oasis and a distant library gathers people who barely know one another. Inside, they feel watched and alone. Fighting the creatures they can see makes the opening more dangerous, and the evidence they find afterward suggests that someone intended it to remain open.

People who answer different calls

The opening recorded on 17, Month of Cala, Year 3 hangs among broken pieces of stone. Darkness lies beyond it, and voices whisper where there should be silence. Manzur sees an evil he cannot leave unanswered, takes up his swords and charges in. Scribonia interrupts his own spell work because someone must close the breach. Myllorpaek enters low and apprehensive.

Jiangshi holds Adelia’s hand as they approach. The women had been preparing to travel; now Adelia asks who is coming to answer the new danger. Inside, Jiangshi greets Scribonia with pleasure, while Adelia asks whether his studies have prepared him for the creatures ahead. He says he has not seen them before. Experience makes him willing to investigate, not already knowledgeable about everything here.

Manzur introduces himself as a champion of the elements and offers the protection of staying near him. Adelia raises her Beacon of Hope staff and asks the others to keep close. They exchange protective magic and practical requests before the fight. Myllorpaek, trying to concentrate, finds Scribonia’s conversation unbearable; Scribonia finds his interruption rude. They have assembled a company without becoming a harmonious one.

The eye beneath them

Beyond the threshold, the sounds of home seem to belong to someone else’s memory. Cold twilight gives way to black mist, and each traveler encounters unsettling impressions drawn from somewhere within. The narration places an enormous eye beneath them, difficult to locate yet impossible for their bodies to ignore.

The companions can see one another and still feel alone. Manzur responds by loudly declaring his intention to cleanse the place. Myllorpaek fears that the noise may awaken what is watching. Scribonia moves forward confidently, accepting a loneliness he already knows. Their reactions give the same landscape different meanings.

Masses of limbs, clawed flesh-hungry creatures and a repeatedly changing form emerge as the immediate threats. An elongated arm drags Manzur closer, and another attack leaves him impaled and badly hurt. Adelia is deafened by the sound of the limbs. Something probes Jiangshi’s mind, but the narrator records no further effect from that attempt. The feeling of being studied has become a fight against bodies they can reach.

The breach becomes unstable

Scribonia brings down meteors. One strikes the eye. Cracks spread through the breach, and a wave of force tears stone into the air. For an instant the fragments hang weightless; then they burst outward as sharp debris while arcane energy surges through the space.

The assault breaks Manzur’s immediate captor, allowing him to move back toward the others, heal himself and raise a ward. It has also made the battlefield itself convulse. The company cannot treat a powerful attack as something with consequences only for its intended target.

A surviving creature advances on Scribonia and tries to sever his connection with his own mind. Its strikes fail to accomplish that. His attempt to reach it telepathically meets a wall of thought. He considers trying to break through, then chooses to concentrate on breaking the enemy instead. Neither failed approach gives the travelers a complete explanation of what they face.

Fears given a fighting shape

The changing creature briefly takes the form of Manzur’s and Scribonia’s worst nightmares. Manzur’s reaction reaches back toward a former state he desperately refuses to endure again. The shape is a weapon used against him, not independent proof that the feared transformation is happening.

The enemy slips toward Adelia and keeps striking. Myllorpaek is also pursued. Burned and carrying fragments of the bombardment, one opponent remains standing longer than the company expects. Manzur answers with fire from his blades, while Adelia tells her attacker she will return. Her defiance is what she believes and promises in the fight, not a guarantee newly established by the breach.

When the final creature falls, the rift begins to shake again. The eye is unstable, and the travelers are told to get out. Adelia heals the company before the scattered survivors move. Manzur admits he is not sure he would have lived without them; Myllorpaek is astonished that they are alive at all. The people who entered with such different manners have depended on one another to reach this moment.

The altar and the map

Not everyone leaves as soon as the fighting ends. Scribonia teleports to places untouched by the battle. Manzur is drawn toward the statues, whose detailed armor and cloaks make them look like carefully made memorials. Jiangshi flies toward another area to investigate before returning to Adelia.

The search uncovers a black-stone altar among the lingering smells of incense, blood and wax. Crimson flames move without a wind. Carved channels and a summoning pattern connect the ritual objects. These are signs of repeated work in the place, rather than an explanation supplied only by a frightened traveler.

A map marks the location where the company stands. Around it, increasingly frantic notes refer to the boundary’s weakness, a confirmed alignment and the possibility of sustaining the breach. The narrator explicitly identifies the opening as planned. The findings establish preparation for this particular rift; they do not identify every planner or explain the cause of every other tear in Fenumion.

Scribonia cuts through stone beneath a circle before departing through a rift of his own. The scene does not establish that his cut alone closes the breach or that he has solved the ritual’s whole design. Investigation has produced evidence, but the collapsing space will not give him unlimited time to understand it.

The last ways out

Small tears open as the larger space fails. Myllorpaek sees the eye blink and takes it as a possible sign of approval. He steps into one of the openings. The interpretation remains his; the blink does not name the being he thinks may be watching.

Falling statues reveal a desert through another tear. Manzur recognizes his way back to the oasis and takes it, wishing the others well. He has heard unfamiliar names and plans during the encounter, but has not suddenly acquired the older adventurers’ shared history.

Adelia and Jiangshi tell Scribonia of intended travel to Prima. Their departure together is witnessed; every later leg of that plan is not. Jiangshi asks whether Adelia is ready, and Adelia holds out her hand. After the battle’s isolation, they leave with the same closeness with which they approached it.

Evidence carried out of a failing place

The expedition changes the question from what might lie beyond a rift to who has been preparing one. An altar, a map and the narrator’s explanation establish deliberate work on this breach. That discovery is narrower than naming a single architect for all the openings, and more useful than treating the entire experience as a meaningless nightmare.

Survival depends on several different acts: Manzur endures the first close assault, protective magic and Adelia’s healing support the company, Scribonia’s bombardment changes the battle at a dangerous cost, and the investigators keep looking after the enemies fall. The ways out are taken under pressure. What remains beyond them is not a fully understood realm. Read the evidence about what sustains particular rifts →
